title: SDK error UX map, actionable messages, and idempotency/resume guidance
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Goal: Deliver a cross-language SDK error surface that gives engineers clear, actionable guidance at runtime and in logs. This ticket synthesizes prior design work and produces: 1) a canonical error taxonomy (families + retry semantics), 2) example error payloads and human-friendly messages for Python/TS/Go, 3) streaming resume semantics and resume-token lifecycle guidance, and 4) recommended telemetry keys and documentation snippets for end-users.

Background: We have a proliferation of ad-hoc error messages across SDKs. Users report uncertainty about when requests are safe to retry, how to resume long-running/streaming responses, and when to consult support. This leads to support load and higher client-side complexity. The deliverables below are intended to reduce ambiguity and give SDK authors a single pattern to implement across languages.
acceptance_criteria: A concise error taxonomy (Transient | Permanent | Client | RateLimit | Auth | Validation | StreamResume) is documented and reviewed
Representative SDK exception classes and interface shapes provided for Python, TypeScript, and Go (code samples included)
Retry guidance table mapping error families -> recommended retry strategy (none / exponential with jitter / idempotent-only / backoff-until-UTC)
Streaming resume protocol documented: resume token encoding, TTL, server-side ops required to support resume, client-side best practices
Console/metrics guidance: recommended telemetry fields (error_code, retryable, idempotency_key, resume_token_present) documented
Internal RFC and implementation PRs opened for each SDK repository with passing CI and integration smoke tests
Migration notes for customers and changelog entries drafted
tasks: Draft canonical error taxonomy and mapping to HTTP status codes
Author Python example exceptions and traceback-friendly messages
Author TypeScript error classes and helpful developer hints
Author Go error types (wrapping patterns) and example usage
Design streaming resume token format and expiry semantics with backend engineers
Add telemetry keys and log message templates to observability docs
Create small integration tests demonstrating retry + resume in e2e harness
Collect review feedback from SDK maintainers and update RFC

proposal_summary: We propose a small, opinionated surface that SDKs implement: a top-level exception type with structured fields: error_code (stable string), message (developer-friendly), retryable (boolean), idempotency_required (boolean), resume_token (optional), and metadata (map of strings). For each language: idiomatic types and helper APIs will be provided. We'll include explicit developer hints in messages (e.g., 'retryable: true; suggested backoff: exponential, max 30s; see https://redwood.ai/sdk/retries').
examples:
Python example:
from redwood import RedwoodError, RetryableError, RateLimitError

try:
    client.generate(prompt)
except RetryableError as e:
    # e.error_code == 'runtime/temporarily_unavailable'
    # e.retryable == True
    logger.info(f"Retryable: {e.error_code} (suggested backoff: 2s -> 30s)")
    sleep_and_retry()
except RateLimitError as e:
    # e.message: 'Rate limit exceeded; quota resets in 29s. See https://redwood.ai/docs/quotas'
    show_user_notice(e.message)

Streaming resume token (human-readable example): 'rwd:rt:v1:expiry=2025-02-20T15:04Z:signature=...'
Client guidance: include resume_token when reconnecting; server may refuse resume if model state changed. Always fall back to full re-request if resume rejected. Limit resume attempts to avoid amplification.
notes_and_tradeoffs: String-based error_code chosen over numeric codes for extensibility and readability in logs
We avoid exposing internal stack traces in messages; SDKs should provide sanitized developer_hint fields for troubleshooting
Resume tokens are best-effort: simpler for users but can mask server-side state churn. We include TTL and recommend clients treat resume as optimization, not guaranteed contract
Idempotency keys for non-idempotent operations reduce accidental retries but require API surface changes and backend idempotency storage; recommend opt-in pattern for GA
